title: Tree From Parent-Child Records
statement:
A binary tree with distinct node values was described as a list of records. Each record [parent, child, isLeft] says that the node with value child is the left child of the node with value parent if isLeft is 1, and its right child if isLeft is 0.

The records come in no particular order, and together they describe one valid binary tree. Build that tree and return its root.

examples.why: 10 has 4 on the left and 7 on the right; 2 hangs to the right of 4.
The first record's parent is not the root. 1 is the root because it never appears as a child.
A root with a single left child.

constraints: The records describe one valid binary tree
hints: Records can mention a node as a child before you have seen it as a parent. How do you make sure each value gets exactly one node object?
Keep a map from value to node, creating a node the first time any record mentions the value. Then each record is one pointer assignment.
The root is the only value that never appears as a child. Keep a set of children.

explain.intuition:
Each record is a single pointer assignment, parent.left = child or parent.right = child. The only difficulty is that the records are shuffled, so you need a way to reach a node by its value no matter which record mentions it first. A hash map from value to node does exactly that: get-or-create the node for both values, then link them.

Finding the root is a membership question. Every node except the root is somebody's child, so the root is the one parent value that never shows up in the children set. It is the same as rebuilding a DOM tree from a flat list of { id, parentId } rows.
steps: Create an empty map nodes and an empty set children.
For each record, get or create the nodes for parent and child, attach the child on the side given by isLeft, and add child to children.
Scan the records again and return the node of the first parent not in children.
pitfalls: Assuming the first record's parent is the root. In the second example it is not.
Creating a fresh node every time a value appears. The tree then falls apart into disconnected copies.
Mixing up the flag: 1 means left, 0 means right.

solutions.title: Children lists, then build from the root
solutions.idea: Store left and right child values per parent and each node's parent. Climb from any value to the top to find the root, then build the nodes level by level.

solutions.title: Value-to-node map plus a children set
solutions.idea: Get or create both nodes for every record and link them. The root is the parent value that never appears as a child.

followups: The records may be invalid: a node with two parents, two roots, or a cycle. How would you detect each case?
Do the reverse: turn a tree into records so that rebuilding it gives the same shape.
